summary: Intermittent SF HQ Wi-Fi disconnects and corporate VPN DNS resolution failures (split-tunnel)
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple SF office users report intermittent Wi-Fi disconnects over the past 48 hours. Users who subsequently reconnect via the corporate VPN experience DNS resolution failures for internal services (e.g., vault.redwood.local, internal-console.redwood.local). Root cause unknown; appears correlated with a configuration change on the office firewall or DHCP/DNS behavior when clients switch networks.

Impact:
- ~12-18 users affected sporadically during business hours (engineering, sales desks on 4th floor).
- Developers cannot access internal-only services after connecting to VPN until DNS cache/route is cleared or laptop rebooted.
- Productivity impact: medium-high during intermittent windows.

Environment:
- SF HQ office Wi-Fi (SSIDs: Redwood-Employee, Redwood-Guest) managed by Meraki MS/ MR stack behind Palo Alto PA-5260 firewall.
- Corporate VPN: OpenVPN server cluster (private), split-tunnel enabled for internet traffic; internal subnets routed via VPN.
- Timeframe first reports: 2026-03-09 09:40 PST.

Observed behavior:
- Wi-Fi disconnects: client reports 'Disconnected' then reconnects to same SSID; DHCP lease renewals logged on Meraki controller.
- After rejoin and VPN connect: client resolves public DNS but not internal short names; nslookup against 10.0.0.10 (internal DNS) times out intermittently.
- Some clients require ipconfig/flushdns + dhclient restart or full reboot to restore internal name resolution.

Expected behavior:
- Seamless reconnection to Wi-Fi and VPN without loss of internal DNS resolution; split-tunnel should still route internal domains to 10.0.0.10 DNS.

Temporary workaround:
- Instruct affected users to run: "sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches" (Linux) or "ipconfig /flushdns" (Windows) and then restart the VPN client. Reboot if that fails.

Notes about scope:
- Guest SSID is unaffected. Wired clients do not report issues. Problem appears tied to Wi-Fi client state transitions and DNS server reachability immediately after VPN bring-up.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Connect a laptop to Redwood-Employee SSID in SF HQ (4th floor).
2) Authenticate and obtain DHCP lease.
3) Establish OpenVPN connection with split-tunnel enabled.
4) Attempt to resolve an internal hostname (vault.redwood.local) or access internal-console URL.
5) If Wi-Fi disconnects and reconnects during the session, note DNS failures immediately after reconnection.

Observed: DNS timeouts or NXDOMAIN for internal names until local cache cleared or network restarted.
logs:
Meraki event snippets (times in PST):
- 2026-03-09T09:38:12: Client AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF association failure: DHCP timeout
- 2026-03-09T09:38:19: Client AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF re-associated, DHCP assigned 10.88.45.102

OpenVPN client log (example):
- Tue Mar 09 09:39:05 2026 ERROR: RESOLVE: Cannot resolve host address: 10.0.0.10: DNS lookup failed
- Tue Mar 09 09:39:07 2026 NOTE: sequence of routes added: 10.0.0.0/16 -> tun0
- Tue Mar 09 09:39:08 2026 WARNING: DNS push failed, fallback to system resolver

System DNS resolution trace (from affected laptop):
- dig +short @10.0.0.10 vault.redwood.local -> ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
- dig +short @1.1.1.1 vault.redwood.local -> 203.0.113.50 (public) -> incorrect; internal name leaked to public resolver
investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-10: Support confirmed 12 initial reports from SF; reproduced on MacBook Pro (macOS 13.6) and Ubuntu 22.04.
- Hypothesis 1: Meraki controller DHCP reassignments are briefly dropping local route advertisement; clients rebind with DNS search domain lost.
- Hypothesis 2: Palo Alto firewall policy update (2026-03-09 02:00 UTC) altered NAT rules for split-tunnel, causing internal DNS traffic to be NATed to public interface resulting in dropped packets.
- Collected packet captures from affected client (pcap attached to INT-4102) showing DNS queries leaving tun0 but no replies from 10.0.0.10 during failure window.
- Verified OpenVPN server config pushes DNS 10.0.0.10 and route 10.0.0.0/16; server logs show successful push but some clients log 'DNS push failed'.
- Meraki telemetry shows spikes in DHCP handshake failures coincident with the times users reported drops (see Meraki dashboard link).
- Quick test: creating a temporary static DNS entry in laptop /etc/hosts allowed access to internal-console immediately after reconnect, indicating name resolution is primary failure, not routing entirely.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10 10:02 PST): Notified office support desk to collect affected MACs and seat locations. Pls escalate to networking team - several engineers blocked.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-10 11:45 PST): I pulled PA firewall audit logs for 2026-03-09 01:30-03:30 UTC. Found a config commit at 2026-03-09 02:05 UTC titled 'egress nat policy tweak' by network-admin. Will coordinate rollback window.

Morgan Chen (SRE) (2026-03-10 12:10 PST): Packet captures received (linked INT-4102). I see DNS queries to 10.0.0.10 with no response; traceroutes show tun0 present. Suggest testing with split-tunnel disabled to confirm whether issue is DNS over VPN only.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-11 09:08 PST): Rolled back the egress NAT change in a controlled window (09:00-09:15 PST). Post-rollback initial checks show fewer DNS timeouts; monitoring continues.

Riley Brooks (Office IT) (2026-03-12 16:20 PST): Collected additional user reports after rollback — two users still had problems after afternoon hotspot maintenance. We swapped APs for those desks; both recovered. Could be flaky AP and concurrent firewall change made it visible.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-14 08:39 PST): Follow-up: request to schedule a deeper config audit for Meraki <-> Palo Alto interactions and to add a health-check monitor for internal DNS reachability over VPN. Assigned INT-4199 for monitoring task.
next_steps:
1) Run controlled tests with split-tunnel disabled on a set of affected clients to confirm DNS behavior (SRE + Networking).
2) Audit Meraki DHCP lease churn on 4th floor APs and check for firmware updates; replace flaky APs (Office IT).
3) Add active health check that queries internal DNS (10.0.0.10) over VPN for SF office and alert on failures (Monitoring / Observability).
4) Create a firewall rule test plan: replay NAT change in staging and validate DNS packet handling (Network team).
5) Follow-up ticket INT-4199 created for long-term monitoring and INT-4200 for Meraki firmware rollout.
resolution: In progress - temporary rollback of egress NAT rule reduced incidents. Ongoing follow-ups: AP replacements and DNS health-checks scheduled. No permanent root-cause confirmed yet.
